admission: All four findings were real. Two of them (LEVEL6 and CRLF) were fixtures that did not contain what they claimed, so the tests were passing on the wrong input - the same escape-layer defect that broke this generator three times. That is now written up as TT-R14-039.

changes.finding: LEVEL6_COVERAGE - an implementation that drops level-six headings passed
changes.fix: the heading fixture now contains levels 1 through 7, the expectation counts only levels 1..6 (ATX), and the test asserts that the seven-hash line is NOT reported as a heading

changes.root_cause: the generated 'CRLF' fixture contained only LF: the escape layer ate the \r, so a program that counts \r as well produced the same number
changes.fix: the fixture now writes real CRLF and asserts its own precondition (assertIn(b'\r', data)) before asserting the census
changes.evidence: mutation (count \n + count \r) fails with an AssertionError

changes.finding: G2_INVOCATION_MISMATCH - crashes under the test's conditions could still count as caught
changes.fix: the probe now runs with the same cwd and the same TS23_MODULE environment as the test; the test's own stdout is classified, and an assertion whose message embeds a traceback is treated as crash_not_evidence, never as a catch
changes.evidence: self-test with a deliberate ZeroDivisionError mutant: caught=false, crash_not_evidence=true, false_red=true, harness exit 1

changes.finding: CACHE_BINDING - a same-size edit within one mtime tick could be hidden by a stale .pyc
changes.fix: __pycache__ is purged before and after every mutation and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 is set for probe and test
changes.evidence: the mutation that previously needed forcing now applies on a plain run

related_tt: TT-R14-039 - fixture must assert its own precondition, otherwise it lies for the test
claim_ceiling: Four reviews, four sets of real findings, all fixed. This is still my measurement, not M2. A fifth independent read is required; if it finds another hole, the honest response is another fix, not a claim that four rounds is enough.
